status: Explicit opt-in handler plus outer response boundary tested; no bootstrap registration or API acceptance
scope: Server-owned exact request scope closure. Final exception response normalization replaces earlier render callbacks/exception-owned render responses with fixed Problem shape. Successful and outside-scope requests retain behavior.
reporting: Within scope, ordinary reportable exceptions are logged with fixed message and only code/status/server correlation UUID; callback stops Laravel default reporting. No exception object, trace, request, user data or raw dependency detail in this callback. Ignored exceptions remain ignored. Earlier/self-reporting exception hooks and external log channels require separate review.
file_dependency: FileSecurityUnavailable maps to safe503 security_state_unavailable; no filenames, keys, provider strings or errors exposed.
router_boundary: FoundationProblemBoundary now normalizes direct controller/inner middleware responses and router-caught HttpResponseException when installed outside the applicable middleware. Error bodies/streams are never read or run; arbitrary headers/cookies are discarded, numeric429 Retry-After only. Unsupported error status maps500. Routes/middleware outside this opt-in boundary remain uncovered until reviewed placement.
composition: Register handler with shared registry only after reviewing the single finalizer and exception reporting hooks. Install response boundary outside all target response-producing middleware. Successful/outside-scope responses retain behavior. Later middleware, direct sends/side effects, custom reporting and host worker lifecycle require acceptance; no universal application redaction claim.
DTO_review: fnd07_problem_contract_v1.json corrections remain proposed. Source OpenAPI is immutable and unchanged; no registration/login/logout/SelfUser implementation or institutional approval invented.
activation: Requires approved API scope/DTOs, response-boundary discipline, log-channel/exception-hook review, authentication and operational security gates. No configuration flag grants acceptance.
registry: Share one FoundationProblemResponses instance with handler and boundary. Weak request-object contexts give each request fresh server correlation even for a reused exception. Private fixed snapshots and sealed outgoing clones prevent downstream mutation from poisoning HTTP bodies or repeated-report logs; repeated normalization retains correlation. No request/response header is a correlation authority.
